outcome: Help pharmacists and clinicians identify medication risks and manage pharmacy demand with evidence-linked, professionally reviewed support.
overview: Prescribing alerts fire constantly and are overridden just as constantly, medication reconciliation is manual at every transition of care, and pharmacy stock swings between expiry write-offs and stockouts. This solution joins EHR, CPOE, pharmacy and inventory data to licensed, versioned medicines knowledge, applies patient-locked rules that show the evidence behind every finding, and tiers alerts so pharmacists see what is genuinely actionable. Pharmacists and clinicians approve every intervention, substitution and replenishment order — nothing is prescribed, dispensed or substituted autonomously. A 10–16-week pilot targets better actionable-alert precision, faster reconciliation and verification, and fewer expiry and stockout events.

benefits.text: Improve actionable-alert precision so pharmacists spend review time on genuine medication risk
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Precision depends on formulary completeness, knowledge-source currency and the alert policy the customer approves; measured against a pre-pilot override baseline, with pharmacist judgement always required

benefits.text: Reduce medication reconciliation and order-verification time at transitions of care
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Target to validate against timed reconciliation baselines in the pilot — not a guarantee, and dependent on how complete the incoming medication history is

benefits.text: Reduce selected expiry write-off and stockout measures through forecast-led replenishment
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on inventory-data accuracy and supplier lead-time stability; national shortages remain outside the solution’s control and every replenishment order is approved by a pharmacist

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); prescribing, dispensing and patient-identifiable data stay in the customer tenancy in the reference designs, in line with UAE and Saudi health-data regulations

notFor.situation: No maintained formulary or licensed, versioned medicines knowledge source
notFor.why: Every finding must cite current, licensed evidence; stale or unlicensed knowledge turns a safety tool into a liability

notFor.situation: Expectation of autonomous prescribing, dispensing or therapeutic substitution
notFor.why: The source catalogue makes no autonomous claim; prescribing, dispensing and substitution stay with the responsible professional, and local health-authority requirements (DHA/DoH/SFDA/MOH) govern anything that would change that

notFor.situation: Prescribing and dispensing records that cannot be reliably tied to a single patient encounter
notFor.why: Wrong-patient or wrong-context findings are the highest-severity failure mode in medication safety; hard patient and encounter identifiers are a precondition

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer owns the formulary, the alert policy and professional accountability for every intervention · Duration: 10–16-week pilot; 20–32 weeks to scaled deployment
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, clinical-informatics engineer, integration engineer, data scientist; customer chief pharmacist, medication-safety officer, pharmacy supply-chain manager, EHR and pharmacy integration leads, privacy and security approvers · Support model: Business-hours or 24×7 option; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor and knowledge-provider escalation
1) Formulary, knowledge-source and alert-policy discovery
2) EHR, CPOE, pharmacy and inventory integration with identifier proof
3) Rule and tiering calibration against a pharmacist-scored gold set
4) Clinical safety, privacy and security testing including downtime workflow
5) Controlled pilot with weekly medication-safety review
6) Stabilisation, benefit review and handover
deliverables: Clinical and pharmacy gold-set evaluation meets the agreed precision thresholds
Zero wrong-patient or wrong-encounter findings across integration and pilot testing
Every finding carries a cited, in-date knowledge source with its version recorded
100% of interventions and replenishment orders show professional approval
Inventory reconciliation, downtime workflow and security tests passed; pharmacists complete UAT
